newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Opel Nederland confirms EU searched its offices.
newsitem.headline: Opel Nederland confirms EU searched its offices.

text.p: Opel Nederland, the Dutch subsidiary of Germany's Adam Opel AG, confirmed on Monday that EU officials had searched its offices in Sliedrecht and the premises of an independent Dutch Opel dealer late last year.
Opel Nederland spokesman Jan-Willem Vester declined to comment on the reason for the searches, held in December, and said the EU had not yet informed the company of its findings.
Parent company Adam Opel AG -- a unit of General Motors -- had said on Friday that the offices of Opel Nederland and one of its Dutch dealers had been searched by the EU.

News of the raids emerged as the European Commission reported that consumers seeking to buy cars cheaply in one EU country and import them to another EU country where prices were higher were facing obstacles.
The Commission said such "parallel imports" were being blocked in Germany, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands.
Vester said Opel dealers in the Netherlands were independent and were therefore free to sell cars to whoever they wanted.
Asked if they might decide not to sell cars to certain customers he said: "I do not see how it is in their own interest not to sell to someone."
Opel Nederland itself had not placed any obstacles in the way of consumers seeking to buy Opel cars, he added.
